items.a: Model answer: Four main functions of the nucleus: (1) It controls all the activities of the cell, because it contains the genetic information (DNA). (2) It stores the hereditary material as chromatin/chromosomes and passes it to daughter cells during cell division. (3) It makes ribosomal RNA and ribosome subunits in the nucleolus and controls protein synthesis by making mRNA. (4) It controls growth, metabolism and reproduction of the cell; its envelope with pores regulates the exchange of material with the cytoplasm.

items.a: Model answer: Peroxisomes (microbodies) are small single-membrane organelles found in plant and animal cells, most common in the liver and kidney cells of animals. They are like lysosomes but denser and have different enzymes, such as catalase, which breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen and protects the cell from its harmful effect. items.q: Cell is called structural and functional unit of life. Justify the statement.
items.q2: خلیے کو زندگی کی ساختی اور فعلی اکائی کہا جاتا ہے۔ اس بیان کا جواز پیش کریں۔
items.q3: حجره د ژوند جوړښتي او دندیزه واحد بلل کېږي. دا بیان ثابت کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: The cell is the structural unit because all living organisms, from bacteria to humans, are built of one or more cells, and tissues, organs and organ systems are made of cells. It is the functional unit because every life process (respiration, digestion, synthesis of protein, excretion, reproduction) takes place within cells with the help of their organelles. A cell can live and reproduce independently when supplied with nutrients (a unicellular organism or a tissue culture), and new cells arise only from existing cells.

items.a: Model answer: Without the cell membrane the cell would die. The membrane controls what enters and leaves, so the cytoplasm would lose its contents and the ions, water and nutrients could not be balanced; the cytoplasm would leak out and the cell would swell or shrink by osmosis; it could not receive signals or keep its internal environment constant and would not be separated from its surroundings.

items.q3: د پروکاریوټیک او یوکاریوټیک حجرې ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Prokaryotic cell: no true nucleus (DNA lies free in the nucleoid), no membrane-bound organelles, small ribosomes (70S), cell wall of murein, size 1-10 micrometres, single circular DNA, binary fission; examples bacteria and cyanobacteria. Eukaryotic cell: a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear envelope, membrane-bound organelles (mitochondria, ER, Golgi), larger ribosomes (80S), size 10-100 micrometres, several linear chromosomes, mitosis/meiosis; examples are plants, animals, fungi and protists.

items.q: Describe the fluid mosaic model of plasma membrane.
items.q2: پلازما جھلی کے سیال پچی کاری ماڈل کو بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د پلازما غشا د سیال موزاییک ماډل تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: The fluid mosaic model of Singer and Nicolson (1972) says the plasma membrane is a fluid double layer (bilayer) of phospholipids in which proteins float like a mosaic. The phospholipid heads are hydrophilic and face the water outside and inside, the tails are hydrophobic and face each other inside. Integral proteins go across the bilayer (channels, carriers) and peripheral proteins lie on the surface; cholesterol keeps the fluidity; carbohydrates attached to proteins or lipids (glycoproteins, glycolipids) lie on the outer surface for recognition. Lipids and proteins can move sideways, so the membrane is fluid.
items.e: Unit 1 plasma membrane.

items.q3: د ګولجي اپارات په اړه تاسو څه پوهېږئ. دندې یې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi complex) is a stack of flattened membrane sacs (cisternae) with vesicles at the edges, with a cis (receiving) face near the ER and a trans (shipping) face. Functions: it modifies, sorts and packs proteins and lipids made in the ER (adds sugar to make glycoproteins), forms secretory vesicles for export (enzymes, hormones), forms lysosomes, makes cell wall material in plants, and forms the plasma membrane.

items.q: Explain critically the role of lysosomes in human body.
items.q2: انسانی جسم میں لائسوسومز کے کردار کی تنقیدی وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: د انسان په بدن کې د لایزوزومونو رول په انتقادي ډول تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Lysosomes are single-membrane sacs full of hydrolytic enzymes. Roles in the human body: (1) Digest food particles and bacteria taken in by white blood cells (phagocytosis), helping defence. (2) Autophagy: break down worn-out organelles and recycle their parts. (3) Autolysis: they burst and digest the cell after its death (suicide bags), which helps in removing tissues, e.g. the tail of the tadpole or the tissue of the uterus after birth. (4) If their enzymes are missing, undigested material builds up and storage diseases (e.g. Tay-Sachs disease) occur; if they leak, they harm the cell, as in arthritis.

items.a: Model answer: The cytoskeleton is a network of protein filaments in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. It has three parts: microtubules (tubulin, hollow tubes; form spindle fibres, cilia, flagella, centrioles), microfilaments (actin, thin solid rods; muscle contraction, cytoplasmic streaming and cell movement) and intermediate filaments (strong ropes that hold the nucleus and give strength). It gives shape and mechanical support, anchors organelles, moves materials and the cell itself, and separates chromosomes at cell division.

items.a: Model answer: Tissue culture is growing cells, tissues or organs of a plant or animal in a sterile artificial nutrient medium outside the organism. Main steps: (1) Choose and cut the explant (a small piece of tissue, e.g. a shoot tip) from a healthy plant. (2) Sterilise the explant and work in a sterile environment (laminar flow cabinet) with sterilised instruments. (3) Put it on a sterile nutrient medium (agar with minerals, sugar, vitamins and growth hormones) in a culture vessel. (4) Incubate under controlled temperature and light; the explant forms a mass of undifferentiated cells (callus). (5) Transfer the callus to a medium with suitable hormones to make shoots and roots (differentiation). (6) Harden the small plants and transfer them to soil.
items.e: Unit 1 tissue culture.

items.a: Model answer: The organelles work as a team. The nucleus holds the instructions (DNA) and makes mRNA; ribosomes make proteins; the ER and Golgi apparatus fold, modify, sort and ship them; mitochondria make ATP by respiration to power all the work; lysosomes and peroxisomes digest and remove waste; the plasma membrane controls entry and exit; in plants chloroplasts make food. Because they cooperate, the cell grows, repairs itself, takes in nutrients and removes waste, and all the cells together keep the body alive.

items.a: Model answer: Water is important for life because of its properties: it is a polar molecule that forms hydrogen bonds. (1) A universal solvent, so reactions and transport in cells occur in water. (2) High specific heat capacity, so temperature of cells and the body changes slowly. (3) High heat of vaporisation, so sweating and transpiration cool organisms. (4) Cohesion and adhesion, which pull water up the xylem and give surface tension. (5) It is a reactant in hydrolysis and photosynthesis. (6) Ice floats, so lakes freeze from the top and aquatic life survives. (7) Transparent, so light reaches aquatic plants.

items.a: Model answer: Watson and Crick (1953) proposed that DNA is a double helix: two polynucleotide strands wound round each other like a twisted ladder with a right-handed turn. The sugar-phosphate backbones are on the outside, run in opposite directions (antiparallel), and the nitrogenous bases face inward and are joined by hydrogen bonds: adenine pairs with thymine (two bonds) and guanine with cytosine (three bonds), so one strand is complementary to the other. The helix is about 2 nm wide and makes one complete turn every 3.4 nm (10 base pairs). This structure explains how DNA copies itself (semi-conservative replication).

items.a: Model answer: Every enzyme has an optimum pH at which it works best (pepsin about 1.5-2, trypsin about 8, salivary amylase about 6.8). A change of pH changes the charges on the amino acids at the active site and the bonds that hold the protein's shape; the active site loses its shape, substrate cannot bind, and the rate falls. An extreme pH denatures the enzyme permanently. The cell therefore keeps its pH nearly constant with buffers.

items.a: Model answer: Characteristics of enzymes: (1) They are globular proteins. (2) They are biological catalysts: they speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy. (3) They are needed in very small quantity and are not used up. (4) They are specific: one enzyme acts on one substrate or a group of related substrates. (5) They work at an optimum temperature and pH and are denatured by heat. (6) They can work in both directions of a reversible reaction. (7) Their activity is controlled by inhibitors and activators. (8) They need cofactors or coenzymes in some cases.

items.a: Model answer: Enzyme inhibition is a decrease in enzyme activity caused by a molecule (inhibitor). Competitive inhibitors look like the substrate, compete for the active site and block it; more substrate can overcome them (malonate on succinate dehydrogenase). Non-competitive inhibitors bind to another site (allosteric site), change the shape of the active site and reduce the activity; extra substrate cannot overcome them (cyanide on cytochrome oxidase, heavy metals Hg and Pb). Inhibition may be reversible or irreversible. Common inhibitors: cyanide, malonate, heavy metals (mercury, lead), penicillin, nerve gases and some drugs and poisons.

items.a: Model answer: Mode of action: (1) The substrate collides with the active site of the enzyme and binds, forming an enzyme-substrate complex. (2) The enzyme strains the substrate bonds (induced fit) and lowers the activation energy. (3) The reaction takes place and the substrate changes to products. (4) The products leave the active site and the free enzyme is ready to combine with another substrate molecule. E + S → ES → E + P.

items.a: Model answer: The question is cut off in the book data; it is answered as "cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation". In the cyclic pathway only photosystem I works: the excited electrons go round through carriers and return to the same chlorophyll, only ATP is made, no NADPH and no oxygen. items.a: Model answer: Sunlight is the source of energy for photosynthesis. Chlorophyll and other pigments absorb photons, which excite electrons in photosystems II and I; this energy is used to split water (photolysis), make ATP and NADPH (light reactions), which are then used to reduce CO2 to sugar. The rate depends on light intensity (up to saturation), colour (red and blue are best) and duration. Without light there are no light reactions, and the dark reactions stop soon after.

items.a: Model answer: Non-cyclic electron pathway: (1) Photosystem II absorbs light; its excited electrons leave P680 and are taken by a primary acceptor. (2) Water is split (photolysis) to replace the lost electrons, giving H+ and oxygen. (3) Electrons pass down an electron transport chain (plastoquinone, cytochromes, plastocyanin) and the energy released pumps protons into the thylakoid space; ATP is made by chemiosmosis. (4) Photosystem I absorbs light and its excited electrons (from P700) are passed through ferredoxin. (5) NADP+ reductase gives them to NADP+, which takes H+ and becomes NADPH. Products: ATP, NADPH and O2.

items.a: Model answer: The Calvin cycle (C3 cycle) in the stroma has three stages: (1) Carbon fixation: CO2 combines with ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP, 5C) with RuBisCO to give an unstable 6C compound that splits into 2 molecules of phosphoglyceric acid (PGA, 3C). (2) Reduction: PGA is reduced to phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL) using ATP and NADPH. (3) Regeneration: most PGAL is rearranged using ATP to make RuBP again; some PGAL leaves to make glucose and other organic compounds. Six turns fix six CO2 and make one glucose.

items.a: Model answer: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. Pyruvate is first oxidised to acetyl-CoA (with NADH and CO2). Steps: (1) Acetyl-CoA (2C) joins oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). (2) Citrate is changed to isocitrate. (3) Isocitrate is oxidised and loses CO2 to form alpha-ketoglutarate (5C) with NADH. (4) Alpha-ketoglutarate loses CO2 to form succinyl-CoA with NADH. (5) Succinyl-CoA gives succinate with one ATP (substrate-level phosphorylation). (6) Succinate is oxidised to fumarate (FADH2). (7) Fumarate is changed to malate. (8) Malate is oxidised to oxaloacetate (NADH), and the cycle repeats. Per turn: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 ATP and 2 CO2.

items.a: Model answer: Some viruses, like HIV, infect and destroy the helper T cells (CD4 lymphocytes), the cells that coordinate the immune response. items.q: List down the main steps in the life cycle of HIV.

items.a: Model answer: Life cycle of HIV: (1) Attachment: the viral glycoprotein (gp120) binds to the CD4 receptor on the helper T cell. (2) Fusion: the viral envelope fuses with the cell membrane and the capsid enters. (3) Reverse transcription: viral RNA is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase. (4) Integration: the viral DNA enters the nucleus and is inserted into the host chromosome by integrase (provirus). (5) Transcription and translation: the host machinery makes viral RNA and proteins. (6) Assembly: new virus particles are assembled. (7) Budding and release: the viruses leave the cell, taking part of the membrane as envelope, and infect other cells.

items.a: Model answer: Lymphocytes are white blood cells that recognise specific antigens. B lymphocytes become plasma cells and make antibodies (humoral immunity) and memory cells. T lymphocytes: helper T cells coordinate the response, cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells (cell-mediated immunity), suppressor T cells stop the response when over, and memory cells give a quick response on a second exposure. Together they remember invaders, destroy them and prevent illness.

items.a: Model answer: A virus protects itself inside the host cell because the antibodies in the blood cannot enter cells. items.a: Model answer: Bacteriophages are used in genetic engineering as vectors (carriers) to carry foreign DNA into bacterial cells. The gene of interest is cut and inserted into the phage genome (for example lambda phage); when the phage infects bacteria it injects the DNA, and the gene is copied or expressed in the host (transduction). Phages are also used in studying genes, in phage display and in phage therapy against bacteria.

items.q: Describe some common control measures against the transmission of HIV.
items.q2: HIV کی منتقلی کے خلاف چند عام کنٹرول اقدامات بیان کریں۔

items.a: Model answer: Control measures against HIV transmission: avoid unsafe sex and keep to one faithful partner (use condoms); use only sterilised or disposable syringes and needles, never share needles or razors; screen all blood and organs before transfusion; infected mothers should take antiviral drugs during pregnancy and delivery and avoid breastfeeding if advised; use gloves when handling blood; health education and early testing. HIV is not spread by touching, sharing food or mosquito bites.

items.a: Model answer: Leaf curl virus of cotton (CLCuV): it is a begomovirus (single-stranded DNA virus) carried by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Symptoms: upward or downward curling of leaves, thickening of veins, enation (small leaf-like outgrowths on the underside of the leaf), stunted growth and few bolls, so the yield falls greatly. items.q: Write a brief note on prions and viroids.

items.a: Model answer: Prions are infectious proteins (proteinaceous infectious particles) with no nucleic acid, discovered by Prusiner. A normal protein of nerve cells (PrPc) is changed to a wrongly folded form (PrPsc) that makes other normal proteins fold in the same way; they form clumps and damage the brain (spongy brain), as in mad cow disease (BSE), scrapie in sheep and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in humans. Viroids are the smallest known infectious agents: small circular single-stranded RNA with no protein coat, found in plants, causing diseases like potato spindle tuber and cadang-cadang of coconut; they don't code for any protein and use host enzymes to copy themselves.
items.e: Unit 5 prions and viroids.

items.a: Model answer: A domain is the highest taxonomic category, above kingdom. The term was coined by Carl Woese (1990) when he found, from rRNA sequences, that living things fall into three major groups: Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. items.a: Model answer: Endospores are thick-walled resting cells that some bacteria (Bacillus, Clostridium) form inside the cell when conditions are bad (drought, heat, lack of food). items.a: Model answer: Genetic recombination is the production of new combinations of genes by the exchange or transfer of genetic material from one cell to another. items.a: Model answer: Bacteria are called nutrient recyclers because saprophytic bacteria decompose dead plants and animals and wastes, and release the minerals, carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus in them back into the soil and air to be used again by plants. Bacteria also convert nitrogen to nitrates (nitrification), and so keep the nutrients cycling in the ecosystem.

items.a: Model answer: Structure of a bacterium (a typical rod-shaped one): a capsule or slime layer (sometimes) outside; a cell wall of murein (peptidoglycan); the plasma membrane; cytoplasm without membrane-bound organelles but containing 70S ribosomes and food granules; a nucleoid, a single circular chromosome of DNA without a nuclear membrane, and often plasmids; mesosomes (infoldings of the membrane); flagella for movement (some); pili/fimbriae for attachment and conjugation. Size is about 1-5 micrometres.

items.q: Discuss various methods of sexual reproduction of a bacteria.
items.q2: ایک بیکٹیریا کی جنسی تولید کے مختلف طریقوں پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: د یوه باکتریا د جنسي تکثیر بېلابېلې طریقې وڅېړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission; the sexual-like methods (genetic recombination) are: (1) Conjugation: two cells join by a pilus (sex pilus), and a copy of the F plasmid or part of the chromosome passes from the donor (F+) to the recipient. (2) Transformation: a bacterium takes up naked DNA of dead bacteria from its surroundings and includes it into its genome (Griffith's experiment). (3) Transduction: a bacteriophage carries a part of DNA from one bacterium to another. All give new combinations of genes.

items.a: Model answer: Modes of nutrition in bacteria: (1) Autotrophic: photoautotrophs use light (cyanobacteria with water, purple and green sulphur bacteria with H2S); chemoautotrophs use energy of inorganic chemicals (nitrifying bacteria, sulphur and iron bacteria). (2) Heterotrophic: saprotrophs (feed on dead matter), parasites (feed on living hosts, causing disease), and symbionts (live together with benefit, as Rhizobium in legume roots or gut bacteria).

items.a: Model answer: Bacterial diseases of plants: citrus canker (Xanthomonas citri, brown raised spots on leaves and fruit), crown gall (Agrobacterium tumefaciens, tumours on stem and roots), bacterial wilt (Ralstonia and Erwinia: sudden wilting), soft rot of vegetables (Erwinia carotovora), blight of rice (Xanthomonas oryzae), and fire blight of apple and pear (Erwinia amylovora). Control: disease-free seeds, resistant varieties, removal and burning of infected plants, crop rotation, and copper-based sprays.

items.a: Model answer: Fungi reproduce asexually by spores, budding or fragmentation. This is critical because it is fast, it needs only one parent, it produces vast numbers of spores that spread by wind and water and colonise new food sources quickly, and the spores withstand bad conditions. Sexual reproduction occurs less often, when conditions need variation.

items.a: Model answer: Fungi are a threat to crops because many parasitic fungi cause plant diseases: rusts and smuts of wheat, powdery mildew, late blight of potato (Phytophthora, a water mould), leaf spots and wilts. items.a: Model answer: Algae are the main producers of oxygen in the biosphere: phytoplankton in oceans and lakes carry out photosynthesis and produce about half of the world's oxygen. They use up the carbon dioxide and release oxygen to the air and to water, which supports the aerobic life of aquatic animals and keeps the CO2-O2 balance. They also make the food that supports food chains.

items.q3: له همژیوي ژوند (سمبایوسیس) څخه تاسو څه پوهېږئ؟
items.a: Model answer: Symbiosis is a close and long relationship between two different species living together. Types: mutualism (both benefit; lichen of an alga and a fungus, mycorrhiza), commensalism (one benefits, the other is not affected) and parasitism (one benefits at the cost of the other).

items.q: How will you justify the name scavengers given to fungi?
items.q2: فنجائی کو دیے گئے نام صفائی کارکن (اسکیوینجرز) کا جواز آپ کیسے پیش کریں گے؟
items.q3: فنجي ته ورکړل شوي نوم پاکوونکي (سکیوینجر) توجیه به تاسو څنګه کوئ؟
items.a: Model answer: Fungi are called scavengers because most are saprotrophs: they secrete digestive enzymes on dead plants and animals, dung and waste, absorb the digested nutrients, and so decompose dead organic matter and clean the environment, returning minerals to the soil.

items.q: Discuss the medicinal importance of *claviceps purpurea*.
items.q2: *claviceps purpurea* کی طبی اہمیت پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: د *claviceps purpurea* طبي اهمیت وڅېړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Claviceps purpurea (ergot fungus) grows on rye and other cereals and forms hard black sclerotia (ergot). Ergot contains alkaloids, from which drugs are made: ergometrine is used to control bleeding after childbirth and to contract the uterus, ergotamine for migraine, and LSD is a derivative. Eating bread made from ergot-infected grain causes ergotism, a serious poisoning.

items.q3: د خمیر اقتصادي اهمیت وڅېړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Economic importance of yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae): it ferments sugar to alcohol and CO2, used in brewing, wine and industrial alcohol; baker's yeast makes dough rise in bread and cakes; yeast extract is rich in vitamin B and protein (Marmite) and is used in animal feed; it is used in genetic engineering and for making vaccines (hepatitis B) and enzymes (invertase). Some yeasts (Candida) cause disease.

items.q: Describe the salient features of class ascomycota.
items.q2: جماعت ایسکومائکوٹا کی نمایاں خصوصیات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د اسکومایکوټا ټولګي مهمې ځانګړتیاوې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Class Ascomycota (sac fungi): the mycelium is septate; sexual spores (ascospores, usually eight) are formed in a sac-like ascus, often in a fruiting body (ascocarp); asexual reproduction is by conidia. Examples: yeast, Penicillium, Aspergillus, Neurospora, morels, truffles, Claviceps. Many are decomposers, some are parasites, and some form lichens.

items.q: Discuss the general characteristics of fungi.
items.q2: فنجائی کی عمومی خصوصیات پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: د فنجي عمومي ځانګړتیاوې وڅېړئ.
items.a: Model answer: General characteristics of fungi: eukaryotic, non-green, achlorophyllous; heterotrophic (saprotrophic, parasitic or symbiotic) with absorptive nutrition; body of thread-like hyphae forming a mycelium (unicellular in yeast); cell wall of chitin; reserve food as glycogen; reproduction by spores (sexual and asexual); no tissues; most are non-motile; found in soil, wood, food and water.
items.e: Unit 7 fungi.
items.h: Members of which phylum produce a club shaped structure that contains spores? a. Chytridiomycota b. Basidiomycota c. Glomeromycota d. Ascomycota

items.q: Given an account of the class basidiomycota.
items.q2: جماعت بیسیڈیومائکوٹا کا بیان دیں۔
items.q3: د باسیډیومایکوټا ټولګي حساب ورکړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Class Basidiomycota (club fungi): septate mycelium, with a dikaryotic phase that lasts long; sexual spores (basidiospores, usually four) are borne on a club-shaped basidium on a fruiting body (basidiocarp); asexual spores are rare. Examples: mushrooms (Agaricus), toadstools, puffballs, bracket fungi, and rusts and smuts of cereals. Many are edible or are decomposers of wood; some are poisonous (Amanita) or plant pathogens.

items.a: Model answer: Beneficial aspects of fungi: decomposers recycling nutrients; food (mushrooms, yeast bread, cheese like Roquefort, soy sauce); antibiotics (penicillin from Penicillium); organic acids and enzymes (citric acid from Aspergillus); fermentation of alcohol; mycorrhiza which help plant roots take up water and minerals; biological control of insects; and as research organisms.

items.q: Given an account of human and animals diseases caused by fungi.

items.a: Model answer: Fungal diseases of humans and animals: ringworm (tinea) of skin, scalp and nails (Trichophyton, Microsporum); athlete's foot; candidiasis (thrush) by Candida albicans in mouth and vagina; aspergillosis of the lungs; histoplasmosis and cryptococcosis (lung and brain); and mycotoxin poisoning (aflatoxin). In animals: ringworm and lung infections of cattle, aspergillosis of birds. Treated with antifungal drugs (nystatin, clotrimazole, fluconazole).

items.q: Define alternation of generation and give its importance.
items.q2: نسلوں کے تبادل کی تعریف کریں اور اس کی اہمیت بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د نسلونو د تناوب تعریف وکړئ او د هغې اهمیت ورکړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Alternation of generation is the regular alternation of two different phases in the life cycle of a plant: a haploid gametophyte (makes gametes by mitosis) and a diploid sporophyte (makes haploid spores by meiosis). Importance: it combines sexual reproduction (variation by meiosis and fertilisation) with spore formation (large numbers of spores for dispersal), and shows evolution from gametophyte-dominant bryophytes to sporophyte-dominant seed plants.

items.q: What is the role of heterospory in the evolution of seed?
items.q2: بیج کے ارتقا میں ہیٹروسپوری کا کیا کردار ہے؟
items.q3: د تخم په تکامل کې د هیټروسپوري رول څه دی؟
items.a: Model answer: Heterospory is the formation of two kinds of spores, small microspores (male) and large megaspores (female). The megaspore is kept and germinates inside the megasporangium on the parent sporophyte, the female gametophyte is protected and nourished, and the zygote grows into an embryo within it; with an added integument this structure became the ovule and then the seed. So heterospory was a key step in the evolution of the seed habit.

items.q: Differentiate between an antheridium and an archegonium.
items.q2: اینتھیریڈیم اور آرکیگونیم میں فرق کریں۔
items.q3: د انتیریډیم او ارکیګونیم ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: Model answer: The antheridium is the male sex organ of bryophytes and pteridophytes: club-shaped or spherical with a wall of sterile cells, making many motile sperms (antherozoids). The archegonium is the female sex organ: flask-shaped with a swollen venter containing one egg and a neck with canal cells, through which the sperms swim to fertilise the egg.

items.q: Give two differences between bryophytes and tracheophytes.
items.q2: برائیوفائٹس اور ٹریکیوفائٹس کے درمیان دو فرق بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د بریوفایټونو او تراکیوفایټونو ترمنځ دوه توپیرونه ورکړئ.
items.a: Model answer: (1) Bryophytes have no vascular tissue (no xylem or phloem) while tracheophytes have xylem and phloem. (2) In bryophytes the gametophyte is the dominant, independent plant and the sporophyte depends on it; in tracheophytes the sporophyte is dominant and independent. (Also: bryophytes have no true roots, stems or leaves; they need water for fertilisation and stay small.)

items.q: Explain the life cycle of flowering plant.

items.a: Model answer: Life cycle of a flowering plant: the sporophyte (the plant) bears flowers. In the anther, pollen mother cells divide by meiosis to form haploid microspores, which become pollen grains (male gametophyte). In the ovule, the megaspore mother cell divides by meiosis; one megaspore survives and by three mitotic divisions forms the embryo sac with eight nuclei (female gametophyte, including the egg). Pollination brings the pollen to the stigma; the pollen tube grows to the ovule. Double fertilisation: one sperm fuses with the egg (zygote, 2n) and the other with the two polar nuclei (endosperm, 3n). The zygote grows to an embryo and the ovule becomes a seed; the ovary becomes a fruit; the seed germinates into a new plant.

items.a: Model answer: Heart in animals: In invertebrates like annelids there are simple contractile blood vessels (pseudo-hearts); arthropods and molluscs have a tubular or chambered heart in an open system. items.a: Model answer: Annual rings are formed by the vascular cambium. In spring, with plenty of water, the cambium makes wide xylem vessels and thin-walled tracheids (early or spring wood, light in colour). Later in the summer and autumn, as water gets scarce, it makes narrow, thick-walled cells (late or autumn wood, dark in colour). In winter the cambium rests. The next spring, a new layer of wide cells begins, so a clear ring forms every year. Counting the rings shows the age of the tree, and their width shows the climate of each year.

items.a: Model answer: Adaptations of plants to cold: (1) Deciduous plants shed leaves in autumn and become dormant. (2) Buds are covered by scales and the plant is covered with hairs or thick bark for insulation. items.q: Explain the movement of water in xylem through TACT mechanism.
items.q2: زائلم میں پانی کی حرکت کی وضاحت TACT میکانزم کے ذریعے کریں۔
items.q3: په زایلم کې د اوبو حرکت د TACT میکانیزم له لارې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Water moves up in the xylem by the Transpiration-Adhesion-Cohesion-Tension (TACT) mechanism. Transpiration: water evaporates from the leaf mesophyll cells through the stomata; this lowers the water potential in the leaf and creates a tension (negative pressure, a pull). Cohesion: hydrogen bonds hold water molecules together, so the tension pulls the whole water column in the xylem like a continuous thread. Adhesion: water molecules stick to the walls of the xylem vessels, which stops the column from falling and helps capillary rise. Tension: the negative pressure transmitted down the xylem to the roots pulls water in from the soil.
items.e: Unit 10 transport in xylem.

items.q3: په بوټو کې د بورو حرکت تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Model answer: Sugars (mostly sucrose) move through the phloem by translocation, explained by the pressure-flow (mass-flow) hypothesis of Munch. At a source (leaf), sucrose is actively loaded into the sieve tubes with the help of companion cells; water enters by osmosis and raises the pressure. At a sink (root, fruit, growing parts) sucrose is unloaded and used or stored as starch, and water leaves, so pressure falls. The pressure difference pushes the phloem sap from the source to the sink. Movement can be up or down according to the need.

items.a: Model answer: Gastric juice is controlled in three phases. items.a: Model answer: In the small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum) the chyme meets bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal juice (succus entericus). Pancreatic amylase digests starch to maltose; trypsin and chymotrypsin break proteins into peptides; lipase breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol. Intestinal enzymes finish the work: maltase, sucrase and lactase make glucose, fructose and galactose; peptidases make amino acids; nucleases break nucleic acids. Absorption: the inner wall has folds, villi and microvilli which give a huge area; glucose and amino acids are absorbed by diffusion and active transport into the blood capillaries of the villi (and go to the liver by the hepatic portal vein); fatty acids and glycerol enter the lacteal (lymph).

items.a: Model answer: Interstitial (tissue) fluid is formed from blood plasma. At the arterial end of capillaries, the blood pressure is higher than the osmotic pressure, so water and dissolved substances (glucose, amino acids, salts, oxygen) filter out through the thin capillary walls into the spaces between cells, but red blood cells and large proteins stay in. At the venous end most of the fluid returns by osmosis and the rest goes into the lymph vessels.

items.a: Model answer: Allergy is an abnormally strong (hypersensitive) reaction of the immune system to a harmless substance. The substances that cause it are allergens. Common allergens: pollen, dust mites, animal hair, some foods (egg, nuts, fish), drugs (penicillin), insect stings. Common allergic conditions: hay fever (allergic rhinitis), asthma, skin allergies (eczema, hives), food allergies, and anaphylactic shock.

items.a: Model answer: Acquired immunity is of two types. Active immunity: the body makes its own antibodies after being exposed to an antigen, naturally by an infection or artificially by a vaccine; it takes time to start but lasts long and has memory cells. Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies are given to the person, naturally from the mother through the placenta and breast milk or artificially by injecting antiserum; it works at once but is short-lived with no memory.

items.q: What are the main events of inflammatory response?
items.q2: سوزشی ردعمل کے اہم واقعات کیا ہیں؟

items.a: Model answer: Events of the inflammatory response: (1) Tissue damage or infection releases histamine and other chemicals from mast cells. (2) Blood vessels widen and become more permeable, causing redness, heat and swelling, and more blood reaches the area. (3) Phagocytes (neutrophils, then macrophages) leave the capillaries and engulf the germs. (4) Fluid and clotting factors leak out, forming a clot that limits the spread. (5) Pus (dead cells and germs) forms, and the tissue is repaired. The signs are redness, heat, swelling and pain.
items.e: Unit 13 inflammation.

items.a: Model answer: Neutrophils and macrophages are phagocytes. They move to the infection (chemotaxis) and recognise bacteria, often coated with antibodies. They engulf the bacteria by phagocytosis into a vacuole (phagosome); lysosomes fuse with it and their enzymes, together with reactive oxygen compounds, digest and kill the bacteria. Macrophages also show parts of the germ (antigens) to the T cells.

items.a: Model answer: Cell-mediated immunity is carried out by T lymphocytes. An antigen-presenting cell (macrophage) shows the antigen to a helper T cell, which is activated and releases cytokines. These stimulate cytotoxic T cells that multiply, recognise infected cells (or cancer cells), and kill them by releasing perforin and enzymes; some become memory T cells. The helper T cells also help B cells and macrophages.

items.a: Model answer: Transplant rejection: the cells of a transplanted organ carry foreign antigens (the MHC or HLA markers) that are different from the recipient's. The recipient's helper T cells recognise them and activate cytotoxic T cells, which attack and destroy the graft; B cells make antibodies against the graft and macrophages join in. For this reason the donor and recipient are matched and immunosuppressant drugs (cyclosporine) are given, which lower the T-cell activity.
items.e: Unit 13 transplants.

items.a: Model answer: Article: vaccination of newborn infants. In Pakistan the Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) gives free vaccines: BCG (tuberculosis) and oral polio vaccine at birth; at 6, 10 and 14 weeks pentavalent vaccine (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae b), pneumococcal vaccine, rotavirus vaccine and polio (OPV/IPV); measles at 9 and 15 months; tetanus toxoid for mothers. Vaccines make the baby's immune system produce antibodies and memory cells without causing the disease. Chemical nature: BCG is a live weakened bacterium; oral polio and measles vaccines are live attenuated viruses; inactivated polio vaccine is killed virus; diphtheria and tetanus vaccines are toxoids (inactivated protein toxins); hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant surface protein; pneumococcal and Hib vaccines are polysaccharide conjugated to protein.

items.a: A gram atom is the atomic mass of an element in grams and contains one mole (6.022 × 10²³) of atoms. items.a: A balanced chemical equation gives the correct mole ratios of the reactants and products (by the law of conservation of mass), so it is used to find how much of one substance reacts with or forms another. Without balancing, the calculated amounts would be wrong.

items.q3: د ګاز د تخلیې نل څه دی؟ هغه شرایط ولیکئ چې د کتوډ وړانګو د تولید لپاره اړین دي.
items.a: A gas discharge tube is a glass tube with two metal electrodes (cathode and anode) sealed in at the ends and connected to a vacuum pump, in which an electric discharge is passed through a gas at low pressure. Conditions for the production of cathode rays: (1) the gas pressure inside the tube should be very low (about 0.01 torr); (2) a very high voltage (about 5000 to 10000 V) must be applied between the electrodes; then a glow of rays travels from the cathode to the anode.
items.e: Discharge tube experiment.

items.q: Write an equation, which shows the production of neutron from the lighter atoms.
items.q2: ایسی مساوات لکھیں جو ہلکے ایٹموں سے نیوٹران کی پیداوار ظاہر کرے۔
items.q3: داسې معادله ولیکئ چې له سپکو اټومونو څخه د نیوټرون تولید وښيي.
items.a: The neutron was produced by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles (Chadwick, 1932): ⁹₄Be + ⁴₂He → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n.
items.e: A neutron is emitted when light nuclei are hit by alpha particles.

items.q: Looking into the values of r₁, r₂, r₃ and r₄ and r₂ − r₁, r₃ − r₂ and r₄ − r₃ etc. What do you conclude about the spacing between the orbits?
items.q2: r₁، r₂، r₃ اور r₄ کی قدروں اور r₂ − r₁، r₃ − r₂ اور r₄ − r₃ وغیرہ کو دیکھتے ہوئے، مداروں کے درمیان فاصلے کے بارے میں آپ کیا نتیجہ اخذ کرتے ہیں؟
items.q3: د r₁، r₂، r₃ او r₄ ارزښتونو او r₂ − r₁، r₃ − r₂ او r₄ − r₃ او نورو ته په کتلو، د مدارونو ترمنځ د واټن په اړه څه پایله اخلئ؟
items.a: The spacing between the orbits increases as we go away from the nucleus: r₂ − r₁ < r₃ − r₂ < r₄ − r₃. This is because the radius is proportional to n² (rₙ = 0.529 n² Å), so the successive differences (3, 5, 7 times 0.529 Å) grow larger. The orbits are not equally spaced.
items.e: From r = 0.529 n² Å.

items.q: You may also try for E₂ − E₁, E₃ − E₂, E₄ − E₃ and E₅ − E₄ etc. to check what happens to the difference in energies between two successive energy levels (orbits) as you move away from the nucleus?

items.q3: د E₂ − E₁، E₃ − E₂، E₄ − E₃ او E₅ − E₄ او نورو لپاره هم هڅه وکړئ څو وګورئ چې له هستې څخه په لرې کېدو د دوو پرله پسې انرژي کچو (مدارونو) ترمنځ د انرژیو توپیر ته څه پېښېږي؟
items.a: The energy differences get smaller as we go away from the nucleus: since Eₙ = −1312/n² kJ/mol, E₂−E₁ = 984 kJ/mol, E₃−E₂ = 182 kJ/mol, E₄−E₃ = 63.8 kJ/mol, E₅−E₄ = 30.5 kJ/mol. The energy levels come closer together (converge) at larger distances.
items.e: From Eₙ = −1312/n² kJ/mol.

items.a: r = n² h² / (4π² m e² k) = 0.529 n² Å, i.e. rₙ = 0.529 n² Å (for hydrogen, n = 1, 2, 3 ...), where h is Planck's constant, m the mass and e the charge of the electron.

items.a: Eₙ = −2π² m e⁴ k² / (n² h²) = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ / n² J = −1312 / n² kJ/mol = −13.6 / n² eV (n = 1, 2, 3 ...).

items.q2: ہائیڈروجن ایٹم میں الیکٹران تیسرے مدار سے پہلے مدار میں چھلانگ لگاتا ہے۔ طیفی لکیر کی … تعدد اور طول موج معلوم کریں۔
items.q3: د هایدروجن په اټوم کې الکترون له درېیم مدار څخه لومړي مدار ته ټوپ کوي. د طیفي کرښې … فریکونسي او د څپې اوږدوالی محاسبه کړئ.
items.a: ΔE = E₁ − E₃ = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ (1/1² − 1/3²) = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ × 8/9 = 1.94 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Frequency ν = ΔE / h = 1.94 × 10⁻¹⁸ / 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ = 2.92 × 10¹⁵ Hz. Wavelength λ = c / ν = 3 × 10⁸ / 2.92 × 10¹⁵ = 1.03 × 10⁻⁷ m = 103 nm (Lyman series, ultraviolet).
items.e: Spectral line of hydrogen.

items.q3: د کانال وړانګو هرې څلور ځانګړنې، د چارج، کتلې او چارج پر کتلې نسبت په ګډون، بیان کړئ.
items.a: Four characteristics of canal rays (anode rays): (1) they are positively charged particles (positive ions); (2) they travel in straight lines in the opposite direction to the cathode rays; (3) their mass depends on the gas used (hydrogen gives the lightest, about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, the proton); (4) their charge to mass ratio (e/m) depends on the gas and is much smaller than for the electron (for H⁺, 9.58 × 10⁷ C/kg), and they are deflected in electric and magnetic fields towards the negative plate.
items.e: Canal rays were discovered by Goldstein.

items.q: Define spectrum and name its different types.
items.q2: طیف کی تعریف کریں اور اس کی مختلف اقسام کے نام بتائیں۔
items.q3: طیف تعریف کړئ او د بېلابېلو ډولونو نومونه یې ولیکئ.
items.a: A spectrum is the pattern obtained when light is split into its component colours or wavelengths by a prism or grating. Types: emission spectra (continuous and line/atomic or band spectra) and absorption spectra. A continuous spectrum has all the wavelengths (e.g. white light); a line spectrum consists of sharp lines of particular wavelengths (e.g. atomic hydrogen).

items.a: The spectral series of hydrogen: Lyman (n₁ = 1; ultraviolet region), Balmer (n₁ = 2; visible region), Paschen (n₁ = 3; infrared), Brackett (n₁ = 4; infrared) and Pfund (n₁ = 5; far infrared).

items.q: What are the defects of Bohr’s atomic model?
items.q2: بوہر کے ایٹمی ماڈل کی خامیاں کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د بوهر د اټومي ماډل نیمګړتیاوې څه دي؟
items.a: Defects of Bohr's atomic model: (1) it could not explain the spectra of atoms having more than one electron; (2) it did not explain the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field (Zeeman effect) or in an electric field (Stark effect); (3) it could not explain the fine structure of the lines; (4) it did not account for the wave nature of the electron (de Broglie) or the uncertainty principle; (5) it could not explain why only certain orbits are stable.
items.e: Limits of Bohr's model.

items.q: • What are X-rays? Write … its different types.
items.q2: • ایکس شعاعیں کیا ہیں؟ ان کی مختلف اقسام … لکھیں۔
items.q3: • ایکس وړانګې څه دي؟ د هغو بېلابېل ډولونه … ولیکئ.
items.a: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiations with very short wavelength (0.1 to 100 Å), discovered by Röntgen in 1895 when fast cathode rays strike a metal target. Types: (1) soft X-rays (long wavelength, low penetration) and (2) hard X-rays (short wavelength, high penetration); also characteristic X-rays (line spectrum of the target metal) and continuous X-rays (white radiation).
items.e: X-ray types.

items.q: • Define Planck’s quantum … theory and prove that E = hcν̄
items.q2: • پلانک کے کوانٹم … نظریے کی تعریف کریں اور ثابت کریں کہ E = hcν̄
items.q3: • د پلانک کوانتمي … نظریه تعریف کړئ او ثابته کړئ چې E = hcν̄
items.a: Planck's quantum theory: energy is emitted or absorbed by a body not continuously but in small packets called quanta (photons); the energy of one quantum is directly proportional to the frequency of the radiation, E = hν, where h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s. Proof of E = hcν̄: since ν = c/λ, E = hν = hc/λ, and the wave number ν̄ = 1/λ, so E = h c ν̄.
items.e: Planck 1900.

items.q: Reading Check: Define Moseley’s law.
items.q2: مطالعے کی جانچ: موزلے کے قانون کی تعریف کریں۔
items.q3: د لوست ارزونه: د موزلي قانون تعریف کړئ.
items.a: Moseley's law: the square root of the frequency of the characteristic X-rays emitted by an element is directly proportional to its atomic number, √ν = a (Z − b), where a and b are constants. It showed that atomic number (not atomic mass) is the fundamental property of an element.
items.e: Moseley, 1913.

items.q: Reading Check: What are quantum numbers? Write the name of four quantum numbers.
items.q2: مطالعے کی جانچ: کوانٹم اعداد کیا ہیں؟ چار کوانٹم اعداد کے نام لکھیں۔
items.q3: د لوست ارزونه: کوانتمي شمېرې څه دي؟ د څلورو کوانتمي شمېرو نومونه ولیکئ.
items.a: Quantum numbers are the numbers which describe the energy, size, shape and orientation of an orbital and the spin of the electron in it. The four quantum numbers: principal (n), azimuthal or angular momentum (ℓ), magnetic (m or mℓ) and spin (s or mₛ).
items.e: Definition.

items.q: Briefly write the Moseley experiment.
items.q2: موزلے کا تجربہ مختصراً لکھیں۔
items.q3: د موزلي تجربه په لنډ ډول ولیکئ.
items.a: Moseley bombarded different metals as targets in an X-ray tube with cathode rays and measured the frequencies of the X-rays emitted. He plotted √ν against the atomic number Z and obtained a straight line (√ν = a(Z − b)). He concluded that atomic number, the nuclear charge, is the fundamental property determining an element's characteristic X-rays, and used it to arrange the elements and to predict missing elements.
items.e: Moseley's experiment.
items.h: Reading Check: What are quantum numbers? Write the name of four quantum numbers.

items.q: Explain the magnetic quantum number in detail.
items.q2: مقناطیسی کوانٹم عدد کی تفصیل سے وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: مقناطیسي کوانتمي شمېره په تفصیل تشریح کړئ.
items.a: The magnetic quantum number (m) describes the orientation of an orbital in space (the direction of its axis) in an external magnetic field. For a given ℓ it can have (2ℓ + 1) values from −ℓ to +ℓ including 0; e.g. for p (ℓ = 1), m = −1, 0, +1 (three orbitals pₓ, p_y, p_z), for d (ℓ = 2) five values. It explains the splitting of lines in a magnetic field (Zeeman effect).
items.e: Magnetic quantum number.
items.h: Reading Check: What are quantum numbers? Write the name of four quantum numbers.

items.q: What are the shapes of s, p and d orbitals?

items.a: Pauli's exclusion principle: no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers, so an orbital can hold at most two electrons with opposite spins. Hund's rule: in degenerate orbitals (same energy, e.g. p, d) electrons occupy them singly with parallel spins first, and pair up only after each orbital has one electron.

items.q3: د کاتوډ وړانګو هرې څلور ځانګړنې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Four properties of cathode rays: (1) they travel in straight lines, from the cathode; (2) they carry negative charge, being deflected towards the positive plate in electric and magnetic fields; (3) they produce fluorescence and heat and produce X-rays when they strike a metal; (4) they are deflected by magnetic fields and have momentum (they turn a small paddle wheel), and their e/m (1.76 × 10¹¹ C/kg) is the same for every gas.
items.e: Cathode ray properties.

items.q: How will you differentiate between a continuous and a line spectrum?
items.q2: مسلسل اور خطی طیف میں کیسے فرق کریں گے؟
items.q3: د پرله پسې او خطي طیف ترمنځ څنګه توپیر کوئ؟
items.a: A continuous spectrum contains all the wavelengths (colours) of a range merging into each other without gaps, e.g. white light or the light of a heated solid. A line spectrum consists of separate bright lines of definite wavelengths on a dark background, produced by excited atoms, and is characteristic of the element (e.g. hydrogen).
items.e: Difference between spectra.

items.q: How did Moseley discover that the atomic number (Z) is the fundamental property of an element?
items.q2: موزلے نے کیسے دریافت کیا کہ ایٹمی نمبر (Z) عنصر کی بنیادی خصوصیت ہے؟
items.q3: موزلي څنګه کشف کړه چې اټومي شمېره (Z) د عنصر اساسي ځانګړنه ده؟
items.a: Moseley measured the frequencies of the characteristic X-rays of many elements and found that the square root of the frequency varied regularly with a whole-number: the position of the element in the periodic table (atomic number Z), not atomic mass. A graph of √ν against Z for the K-lines was a straight line, so Z (nuclear charge) is the fundamental property.
items.e: Moseley's discovery.

items.q: What are the shortcomings of Bohr’s atomic model?
items.q2: بوہر کے ایٹمی ماڈل کی کمزوریاں کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د بوهر د اټومي ماډل نیمګړتیاوې څه دي؟
items.a: Shortcomings of Bohr's model: it explains only the hydrogen-like (one-electron) species; cannot explain the spectra of multi-electron atoms, the fine structure and the Zeeman and Stark effects; it treats the electron as a particle on a fixed orbit, disregarding the wave nature of the electron and Heisenberg's uncertainty principle; and it gives no explanation of chemical bonding.
items.e: Limits of Bohr's model.

items.q: Can you give the reason that 4s orbital are written first than the 3d orbital.

items.q3: ایا دلیل بیانولای شئ چې 4s اوربیټال ولې له 3d اوربیټال څخه مخکې لیکل کېږي.
items.a: The 4s orbital is filled before 3d because its energy is lower: by the (n + ℓ) rule, 4s has n + ℓ = 4 + 0 = 4 while 3d has 3 + 2 = 5; the 4s orbital penetrates closer to the nucleus and so is more stable at the point of filling.
items.e: Aufbau (n + ℓ) rule.

items.q: (a) What is Planck’s quantum theory? What are the postulates of this theory?
items.q2: (a) پلانک کا کوانٹم نظریہ کیا ہے؟ اس کے مفروضات کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: (a) د پلانک کوانتمي نظریه څه ده؟ د دې نظریې فرضیې څه دي؟
items.a: (a) Planck's quantum theory: a body emits or absorbs energy discontinuously in small packets called quanta (photons). Postulates: (1) energy is emitted or absorbed in whole-number multiples of a quantum; (2) the energy of one quantum is proportional to the frequency of the radiation, E = hν (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s); (3) a body emits or absorbs energy as nhν where n = 1, 2, 3 ...
items.e: Planck.

items.q: (b) Prove that E = hcν̄, where E = energy, h= Planck’s constant, c = velocity of light, and ν̄ = wave number.

items.q3: (b) ثابته کړئ چې E = hcν̄، دلته E = انرژي، h= د پلانک ثابت، c = د رڼا سرعت او ν̄ = د څپو شمېر دی.
items.a: Since frequency ν = c/λ, E = hν = hc/λ. The wave number is ν̄ = 1/λ, so E = hcν̄.
items.e: Proof.

items.q: (a) Write down the main postulates of Bohr’s atomic model.
items.q2: (a) بوہر کے ایٹمی ماڈل کے بنیادی مفروضات لکھیں۔
items.q3: (a) د بوهر د اټومي ماډل اساسي فرضیې ولیکئ.
items.a: Postulates of Bohr's model: (1) an electron revolves around the nucleus in definite circular orbits (stationary states) without radiating energy; (2) an electron can move only in orbits where its angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2π, mvr = nh/2π; (3) energy is emitted or absorbed only when the electron jumps from one orbit to another, ΔE = E₂ − E₁ = hν.
items.e: Bohr's postulates.

items.q3: (b) د nم پوښ د شعاع د محاسبې لپاره د بوهر اټومي ماډل د هایدروجن پر اټوم څنګه پلي کېدای شي؟

items.q: (a) Derive expression using Bohr’s model, for the energy difference (ΔE), frequency (ν) and wave number (ν̄) in hydrogen atom.
items.q2: (a) بوہر ماڈل استعمال کرتے ہوئے ہائیڈروجن ایٹم میں توانائی کے فرق (ΔE)، تعدد (ν) اور عدد موج (ν̄) کے لیے عبارت اخذ کریں۔
items.q3: (a) د بوهر د ماډل په کارولو په هایدروجن اټوم کې د انرژۍ د توپیر (ΔE)، فریکونسۍ (ν) او د څپو شمېر (ν̄) لپاره عبارت راوباسئ.
items.a: With Eₙ = −2π²me⁴k²/n²h², ΔE = E₂ − E₁ = 2π²me⁴k²/h² (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²). Frequency ν = ΔE/h = (2π²me⁴k²/h³)(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²). Wave number ν̄ = ν/c = R_H (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), where R_H = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ (Rydberg constant).
items.e: Derivation from Bohr's energy levels.

items.q: (b) How does Bohr’s model explain the hydrogen spectrum?
items.q2: (b) بوہر ماڈل ہائیڈروجن کے طیف کی وضاحت کیسے کرتا ہے؟
items.q3: (b) د بوهر ماډل د هایدروجن طیف څنګه تشریح کوي؟
items.a: When the hydrogen gas is excited, electrons jump to higher orbits; when they fall back to lower orbits they emit radiation of energy ΔE = hν equal to the difference between the two orbits. Because the orbits have fixed energies, only certain frequencies appear, giving the line spectrum, and the different series (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund) correspond to drops to n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
items.e: Bohr's explanation of the hydrogen spectrum.

items.q: (a) What are X-rays? How are these rays produced?
items.q2: (a) ایکس شعاعیں کیا ہیں؟ یہ کیسے پیدا ہوتی ہیں؟
items.q3: (a) ایکس وړانګې څه دي؟ دا څنګه تولیدېږي؟
items.a: (a) X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiations of very short wavelength. They are produced in an X-ray tube when fast moving electrons (cathode rays) strike a heavy metal target (anode, e.g. tungsten, copper or molybdenum) at a very high voltage: some energy is converted into X-rays.
items.e: Röntgen.

items.q: (b) Enlist some characteristics of X – rays.
items.q2: (b) ایکس شعاعوں کی کچھ خصوصیات درج کریں۔
items.q3: (b) د ایکس وړانګو ځینې ځانګړنې ولیکئ.
items.a: Characteristics of X-rays: (1) they travel in straight lines at the speed of light; (2) they are not deflected by electric or magnetic fields (no charge); (3) they have high penetrating power; (4) they affect photographic plates and cause fluorescence; (5) they ionise gases; (6) they harm living tissue.
items.e: Properties of X-rays.

items.q: (a) Define quantum numbers. What information is given by the … quantum number? What are the possible values for this quant… number?
items.q2: (a) کوانٹم اعداد کی تعریف کریں۔ … کوانٹم عدد کیا معلومات دیتا ہے؟ اس کوانٹ… عدد کی ممکنہ قدریں کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: (a) کوانتمي شمېرې تعریف کړئ. … کوانتمي شمېره څه معلومات ورکوي؟ د دې کوانټ… شمېرې ممکنه ارزښتونه څه دي؟
items.a: (a) Quantum numbers are the set of numbers which describe an electron in an atom. The azimuthal (angular momentum) quantum number ℓ gives the shape of the sub-shell/orbital and the angular momentum; its possible values are 0 to n − 1 (ℓ = 0 for s, 1 for p, 2 for d, 3 for f).
items.e: Quantum numbers.

items.q: (b) What information is given by the magnetic quantum number?
items.q2: (b) مقناطیسی کوانٹم عدد کیا معلومات دیتا ہے؟
items.q3: (b) مقناطیسي کوانتمي شمېره څه معلومات ورکوي؟
items.a: (b) The magnetic quantum number (m) gives the orientation of the orbital in space (the number of orbitals in the sub-shell). Its values are −ℓ ... 0 ... +ℓ, i.e. 2ℓ + 1 values (1 for s, 3 for p, 5 for d, 7 for f).
items.e: Magnetic quantum number.

items.q: (a) What is an orbital? How does it differ from an orbit?
items.q2: (a) اوربیٹل کیا ہے؟ یہ مدار سے کیسے مختلف ہے؟
items.q3: (a) اوربیټال څه دی؟ له مدار څخه څنګه توپیر لري؟
items.a: (a) An orbital is the region of space around the nucleus in which the probability of finding the electron is maximum (about 90-95 %), given by a wave function ψ. An orbit (Bohr) is a definite circular path around the nucleus along which the electron is assumed to revolve; an orbital has shape and is a probability region, while an orbit is a fixed path (two-dimensional); an orbital can hold at most two electrons.
items.e: Difference between orbit and orbital.

items.a: (b) s orbitals are spherical, with an increasing size from 1s to 2s (with nodes); the three p orbitals (pₓ, p_y, p_z) are dumb-bell shaped, along the three axes at right angles, with a node at the nucleus; the five d orbitals have double dumb-bell shapes (d_xy, d_yz, d_zx, d_x²−y²), and d_z² has a dumb-bell with a doughnut (ring) in the middle.

items.q: Reading Check: Write down at least five postulates of the VSEPR theory.
items.q2: مطالعے کی جانچ: VSEPR نظریے کے کم از کم پانچ مفروضات لکھیں۔
items.q3: د لوست ارزونه: د VSEPR نظریې لږ تر لږه پنځه فرضیې ولیکئ.
items.a: Five postulates of VSEPR theory: (1) the shape of a molecule depends on the number of electron pairs (bonding and lone pairs) around the central atom; (2) electron pairs repel each other and arrange themselves as far apart as possible; (3) lone pair-lone pair repulsion > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair; (4) multiple bonds are treated as one electron group; (5) the molecular shape is determined by the positions of the atoms, not the lone pairs.
items.e: VSEPR postulates.

items.q: Reading Check: Define sigma an… pi bonds.
items.q2: مطالعے کی جانچ: سگما او… پائی بندشوں کی تعریف کریں۔
items.q3: د لوست کتنه: د سیګما ا… پای تړونونه تعریف کړئ.
items.a: A sigma (σ) bond is formed by the head-on (end-to-end) overlap of two atomic orbitals along the line joining the nuclei; it is strong and allows free rotation. A pi (π) bond is formed by the sideways (parallel) overlap of p orbitals above and below the bond axis; it is weaker and prevents rotation.
items.e: Definitions.

items.q: Reading Check: What is hybridization?
items.q2: مطالعے کی جانچ: ہائبرڈائزیشن کیا ہے؟
items.q3: د لوست کتنه: هایبرډ کېدل څه دي؟
items.a: Hybridization is the mixing of atomic orbitals of nearly equal energy of the same atom to form the same number of new equivalent orbitals called hybrid orbitals, with a definite geometry (sp, sp², sp³).
items.e: Definition.

items.q: Discuss the structure of BF₃, CH₄ and H₂O on the basis of VSEPR theory.
items.q2: VSEPR نظریے کی بنیاد پر BF₃، CH₄ اور H₂O کی ساخت پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: د VSEPR نظریې پر بنسټ د BF₃، CH₄ او H₂O جوړښت وڅېړئ.
items.a: BF₃: boron has three bond pairs and no lone pair, so the molecule is trigonal planar with 120° angles. CH₄: four bond pairs and no lone pairs, so it is tetrahedral with 109.5°. H₂O: two bond pairs and two lone pairs (four electron pairs), so the shape is bent (angular) with a bond angle of 104.5°, smaller than the tetrahedral angle because the lone pairs repel more strongly.
items.e: VSEPR theory.

items.q: Define resonance? What are the basic conditions for resonance? Discuss the resonance in ozone molecule.
items.q2: ریزونینس کی تعریف کریں۔ ریزونینس کی بنیادی شرائط کیا ہیں؟ اوزون سالمے میں ریزونینس پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: ریزونانس تعریف کړئ. د ریزونانس بنسټیز شرطونه کوم دي؟ د اوزون په مالیکول کې ریزونانس وڅېړئ.
items.a: Resonance is the phenomenon in which a molecule or ion can be represented by two or more Lewis structures that differ only in the positions of electrons, none of which fully describes the molecule; the true structure is a hybrid. Conditions: the contributing structures must have the same positions of atoms, the same number of paired and unpaired electrons, and similar energies. In ozone (O₃), the O=O–O and O–O=O structures are contributors; the two O–O bonds are equal in length (128 pm), intermediate between a single and a double bond.
items.e: Resonance in O₃.

items.q: Write down at least four postulates of the valence bond theory.
items.q2: ویلنسی بندش نظریے کے کم از کم چار مسلمے لکھیں۔
items.q3: د ظرفیتي تړون نظریې لږ تر لږه څلور اصول ولیکئ.
items.a: Postulates of valence bond theory: (1) a covalent bond forms by the overlap of half-filled atomic orbitals of two atoms; (2) each overlapping orbital contains one electron, and the electrons have opposite spins; (3) the greater the overlap, the stronger the bond; (4) the bond lies in the direction of maximum overlap, which gives the molecule its shape; (5) the atoms of the bond share the pair of electrons.
items.e: Valence bond theory (VBT).

items.q: How sigma bond is different from pi-bond. Explain bonding in the molecules of HCl, Cl₂ and O₂.
items.q2: سگما بندش، پائی بندش سے کس طرح مختلف ہے؟ HCl، Cl₂ اور O₂ سالمات میں بندش کی وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: سیګما تړون له پای تړون څخه څنګه توپیر لري؟ په HCl، Cl₂ او O₂ مالیکولونو کې تړون تشریح کړئ.
items.a: A σ bond is formed by head-on overlap along the internuclear axis and is stronger, with free rotation; a π bond is formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals, is weaker and restricts rotation. HCl: the 1s orbital of H overlaps with the 3p orbital of Cl, giving one σ bond. Cl₂: two 3p orbitals overlap head-on, giving one σ bond. O₂: two 2p orbitals form a σ bond by head-on overlap and the other two (parallel) 2p orbitals form a π bond (double bond).
items.e: Sigma and pi bonding.

items.q: What is hybridization? Discuss the sp³, sp² and sp hybridization in different molecules in detail.
items.q2: ہائبرڈائزیشن کیا ہے؟ مختلف سالمات میں sp³، sp² اور sp ہائبرڈائزیشن پر تفصیل سے بحث کریں۔
items.q3: هایبرډ کېدل څه دي؟ په بېلابېلو مالیکولونو کې sp³، sp² او sp هایبرډ کېدل په تفصیل وڅېړئ.
items.a: Hybridization is the mixing of atomic orbitals of the same atom of nearly equal energy to form an equal number of equivalent hybrid orbitals. sp³ (one s + three p): four equivalent orbitals at 109.5° (tetrahedral), e.g. CH₄. sp² (one s + two p): three orbitals at 120° (trigonal planar) with one unhybridized p orbital left for the π bond, e.g. BF₃, C₂H₄. sp (one s + one p): two orbitals at 180° (linear), two unhybridized p orbitals, e.g. BeCl₂, C₂H₂.
items.e: Hybridization.

items.q: What are the shortcomings of VBT?
items.q2: VBT کی خامیاں کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د VBT نیمګړتیاوې کومې دي؟
items.a: Shortcomings of VBT: it cannot explain the paramagnetism of oxygen; it does not explain the bonding in electron-deficient molecules; it considers the electron localised between two atoms (cannot explain delocalised bonding); it does not explain the energy of molecular orbitals, spectra or the colour of compounds.
items.e: Limits of the valence bond theory.

items.q: What evidence can you find that the CO₂ molecule has a linear but the H₂O molecule has an angular structure?

items.q3: کوم شواهد ښيي چې CO₂ خطي او H₂O زاویوي جوړښت لري؟
items.a: CO₂ has no net dipole moment (zero), because the two C=O bond dipoles cancel each other in a linear molecule, while H₂O has a net dipole moment (about 1.85 D) because its two O-H dipoles do not cancel in a bent molecule. Their shapes also follow from VSEPR theory: CO₂ has two bond pairs and no lone pair (180°); H₂O has two bond pairs and two lone pairs (104.5°).
items.e: Dipole moment evidence.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: Give the reason why the O₂ molecule is paramagnetic.
items.q2: وجہ بتائیں کہ O₂ سالمہ پیرا میگنیٹک کیوں ہے۔
items.q3: دلیل ورکړئ چې O₂ مالیکول ولې پارامقناطیسي دی.
items.a: In the molecular orbital configuration of O₂, the last two electrons occupy two separate degenerate π* antibonding orbitals with parallel spins (Hund's rule), so the molecule has two unpaired electrons and is paramagnetic.
items.e: Molecular orbital theory.

items.q3: کوم مفاهیم دا توجیه کوي چې په NH₃ کې د تړون زاویه 107.5° او په H₂O کې 104.5° ده؟
items.a: NH₃ has three bond pairs and one lone pair, H₂O has two bond pairs and two lone pairs. Lone pair-bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, and two lone pairs repel the bond pairs more strongly, so the angle decreases from 109.5° to 107.5° in NH₃ and 104.5° in H₂O.
items.e: VSEPR theory.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: Differentiate between atomic and molecular orbitals.
items.q2: ایٹمی اور سالماتی اوربیٹلوں میں فرق کریں۔
items.q3: د اټومي او مالیکولي اوربیټالونو ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: An atomic orbital belongs to a single atom (one nucleus) and can hold up to two electrons; a molecular orbital is formed by the combination of atomic orbitals of different atoms and belongs to the whole molecule (two or more nuclei). Atomic orbitals are s, p, d and f; molecular orbitals are bonding or antibonding (σ, π, σ*, π*).
items.e: Difference.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: What data was used to conclude that the calculated bond lengths of heteronuclear molecules are always higher than experimental values?
items.q2: یہ نتیجہ اخذ کرنے کے لیے کون سا ڈیٹا استعمال ہوا کہ مختلف ایٹمی سالموں کی حسابی بندشی لمبائیاں ہمیشہ تجرباتی قدروں سے زیادہ ہیں؟
items.q3: د دې پایلې لپاره کوم معلومات کارول شوي چې د ناهم‌هسته‌يي مالیکولونو حساب شوي تړون اوږدوالی تل له تجربه شوو ارزښتونو لوړ وي؟
items.a: Experimental bond lengths of heteronuclear molecules (e.g. HCl, HF) are shorter than the calculated (sum of covalent radii) values, because of the polarity of the bond: the partial ionic character (electronegativity difference) adds attraction and shortens the bond. The data used are the electronegativity values and the measured bond lengths.
items.e: Schomaker-Stevenson correction.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: How would you prove that a sigma (σ)-bond is stronger than a pi (π)-bond?
items.q2: آپ کیسے ثابت کریں گے کہ سگما (σ) بندش پائی (π) بندش سے زیادہ مضبوط ہے؟
items.q3: څنګه به ثابته کړئ چې سیګما (σ) تړون تر پای (π) تړون پیاوړی دی؟
items.a: A σ bond is stronger because its overlap is head-on along the axis, giving the maximum overlap; a π bond is formed by sideways overlap, which is smaller. Evidence: the bond energy of a C-C single bond (σ, 347 kJ/mol) and of the C=C double bond (σ + π, 614 kJ/mol), the π part being about 267 kJ/mol only, which is less than the σ bond; π bonds break more easily in reactions (addition).
items.e: Bond energies.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: What information would you use to support the view that the He₂ molecule does not exist?
items.q2: He₂ سالمہ وجود نہیں رکھتا، اس خیال کی تائید کے لیے آپ کون سی معلومات استعمال کریں گے؟
items.q3: د دې نظر د ملاتړ لپاره به کوم معلومات وکاروئ چې He₂ مالیکول شتون نه لري؟
items.a: He₂ does not exist because its bond order is zero: He₂ would have two electrons in the bonding σ(1s) and two in the antibonding σ*(1s) orbitals, so the stabilisation of the bonding is cancelled by the destabilisation of the antibonding. Bond order = (2 − 2)/2 = 0; noble gas helium exists as single atoms.
items.e: Molecular orbital theory.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: Differentiate between bonding and anti-bonding orbitals.
items.q2: بندشی اور ضدِ بندشی اوربیٹلوں میں فرق کریں۔
items.q3: د تړونکو او ضد تړونکو اوربیټالونو ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: A bonding molecular orbital is formed by the in-phase (constructive) overlap of atomic orbitals, has a high electron density between the nuclei, and lower energy than the atomic orbitals, so it stabilises the molecule. An antibonding molecular orbital is formed by out-of-phase (destructive) overlap, has a node between the nuclei, higher energy, and destabilises the molecule (marked with *).
items.e: MOT.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: Give reason that why the structure of BF₃ is trigonal planar and NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal.
items.q2: وجہ بیان کریں کہ BF₃ کی ساخت مثلثی مستوی جبکہ NH₃ کی مثلثی اہرامی کیوں ہے؟
items.q3: دلیل ورکړئ چې د BF₃ جوړښت ولې مثلثي هوار او د NH₃ مثلثي هرمي دی؟
items.a: BF₃: boron has three valence electrons forming three bond pairs and no lone pair, so VSEPR predicts a trigonal planar shape (sp², 120°). NH₃: nitrogen has three bond pairs and one lone pair (four electron pairs, sp³), so the lone pair pushes the bond pairs together, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape (about 107°).
items.e: VSEPR theory.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: Why are the bond energies of polar molecules higher than those of non-polar molecules?
items.q2: قطبی سالموں کی بندشی توانائی غیر قطبی سالموں سے زیادہ کیوں ہوتی ہے؟
items.q3: د قطبي مالیکولونو د تړون انرژي ولې د غیرقطبي مالیکولونو تر هغې لوړه وي؟
items.a: The bond energies of polar molecules are higher because the electronegativity difference gives partial ionic character: the attraction between the partial charges (δ+ and δ−) adds to the covalent bond strength, so more energy is needed to break the bond than in a pure non-polar covalent bond.
items.e: Polar and non-polar bonds.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: 1(a). Draw Lewis structures for AlCl₃, PH₃ and H₂O. Use VSEPR theory to predict the molecular shapes of these molecules.

items.q3: 1(الف) د AlCl₃، PH₃ او H₂O د لویس جوړښتونه رسم کړئ. د مالیکولونو د شکلونو اټکل لپاره VSEPR تیوري وکاروئ.
items.a: AlCl₃: Al has three bond pairs and no lone pair; trigonal planar (120°), with Cl atoms attached by single bonds (Al: 3 electrons, each Cl 7). PH₃: P has three bond pairs and one lone pair; trigonal pyramidal (about 93.5°). H₂O: oxygen has two bond pairs and two lone pairs; bent (104.5°).
items.e: Lewis structures and VSEPR shapes.
items.h: Reading Check: Define bond order.

items.q: 1(b). What VSEPR notations correspond to molecules that have a bent shape?
items.q2: 1(ب) خمیدہ شکل والے سالموں کے لیے کون سے VSEPR رموز ہوتے ہیں؟
items.q3: 1(ب) د کږې بڼې لرونکو مالیکولونو لپاره د VSEPR کومې نښې کارېږي؟
items.a: A bent (angular) shape corresponds to AX₂E (three electron pairs: two bonding and one lone pair, e.g. SO₂, bond angle about 119°) and AX₂E₂ (four electron pairs: two bonding, two lone pairs, e.g. H₂O, 104.5°).
items.e: VSEPR notation.

items.q: 2(a). Explain how σ and π bonds are similar and how they are different.
items.q2: 2(الف) وضاحت کریں کہ σ اور π بندشیں کس طرح ملتی جلتی اور مختلف ہیں۔
items.q3: 2(الف) تشریح کړئ چې σ او π تړونونه څنګه ورته او څنګه توپیر لري.
items.a: Similarities: both σ and π bonds are covalent bonds formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals, each with a pair of electrons shared between two atoms. Differences: a σ bond is formed by head-on overlap, is stronger, has electron density along the bond axis and rotation is free; a π bond is formed by sideways overlap, is weaker, has electron density above and below the axis and exists only along with a σ bond (double and triple bonds contain π bonds).
items.e: σ and π bonds.
items.h: 1(c). Discuss the different types of overlapping that lead to sigma-bond formation.

items.q: 2(b). Define and explain resonance with a suitable example.
items.q2: 2(ب) ریزونینس کی تعریف کریں اور مناسب مثال سے وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: 2(ب) رېزونانس تعریف او په مناسبه بېلګه یې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Resonance is the representation of a molecule by two or more Lewis structures that differ only in the position of electrons; the real molecule is a resonance hybrid of all of them and is more stable than any contributor. Example: ozone O₃ (O=O–O ↔ O–O=O), or benzene (two Kekulé structures), or the carbonate ion; the bonds have equal lengths intermediate between single and double.
items.e: Resonance.

items.q: 3(a). Explain the HCl, H₂O and N₂ molecules on the basis of valence-bond theory.
items.q2: 3(الف) ویلنس بندش نظریے کی بنیاد پر HCl، H₂O اور N₂ سالموں کی وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: 3(الف) د والنس تړون تیورۍ پر بنسټ د HCl، H₂O او N₂ مالیکولونه تشریح کړئ.
items.a: HCl: the 1s orbital of H (half-filled) overlaps head-on with the half-filled 3p orbital of Cl to form one σ bond. H₂O: the two half-filled 2p orbitals of O overlap with the 1s orbitals of two H atoms to form two σ bonds; angle about 90° by VBT (actual 104.5°). N₂: the three half-filled 2p orbitals of each N overlap: one head-on σ bond and two sideways π bonds, forming a triple bond N≡N.
items.e: Valence bond theory.
items.h: 2(c). Discuss (i) bond energies, (ii) bond length and (iii) ionic character with suitable examples.

items.q: 3(b). Define and explain hybridization with reference to the sp model of hybridization.
items.q2: 3(ب) sp ہائبرڈائزیشن ماڈل کے حوالے سے ہائبرڈائزیشن کی تعریف اور وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: 3(ب) د sp هایبرډایزېشن ماډل په تړاو هایبرډایزېشن تعریف او تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Hybridization is the mixing of orbitals of nearly the same energy of the same atom to give an equal number of equivalent hybrid orbitals. In sp hybridization, one s and one p orbital mix to give two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals, at 180° (linear), with 50 % s-character; e.g. BeCl₂, C₂H₂ (the two unhybridized p orbitals on each carbon form the two π bonds).
items.e: sp hybridization.

items.q: 4(a). Write down the main points of molecular-orbital theory.
items.q2: 4(الف) سالماتی اوربیٹل نظریے کے اہم نکات لکھیں۔
items.q3: 4(الف) د مالیکولي اوربیټال تیورۍ مهم ټکي ولیکئ.
items.a: Main points of molecular orbital theory: (1) atomic orbitals combine to form the same number of molecular orbitals spread over the whole molecule; (2) in-phase combination gives lower energy bonding MOs and out-of-phase combination gives higher energy antibonding MOs; (3) electrons fill the MOs by the Aufbau principle, Pauli's principle and Hund's rule; (4) bond order = (Nb − Na)/2; (5) a stable molecule needs bond order > 0.
items.e: MOT.
items.h: 3(c). Describe how knowledge of molecular polarity can be used to explain some physical and chemical properties of molecules.

items.q: 4(b). Draw the bonding in the oxygen molecule with the help of molecular-orbital theory.
items.q2: 4(ب) سالماتی اوربیٹل نظریے کی مدد سے آکسیجن سالمے کی بندشیں بنائیں۔
items.q3: 4(ب) د مالیکولي اوربیټال تیورۍ په مرسته د اکسیجن مالیکول تړونونه رسم کړئ.
items.a: O₂ has 16 electrons. MO configuration: σ1s² σ*1s² σ2s² σ*2s² σ2p_z² (π2p_x² = π2p_y²) (π*2p_x¹ = π*2p_y¹). There are 10 bonding and 6 antibonding electrons, bond order = (10 − 6)/2 = 2 (double bond), with two unpaired electrons in the π* orbitals, so oxygen is paramagnetic.
items.e: MO diagram of O₂.

items.q: 5(a). How can the geometry of a molecule be determined by using the dipole moment?
items.q2: 5(الف) ڈائی پول مومنٹ استعمال کرکے سالمے کی جیومیٹری کیسے متعین کی جا سکتی ہے؟
items.q3: 5(الف) د ډایپول مومنټ په کارولو د مالیکول هندسه څنګه ټاکل کېدای شي؟
items.a: The dipole moment shows the shape: a molecule with zero dipole moment despite polar bonds must be symmetrical (linear CO₂, trigonal planar BF₃, tetrahedral CCl₄), while a molecule with a net dipole moment is not symmetrical (angular H₂O, pyramidal NH₃). A non-zero value of H₂O (1.85 D) proves the bent structure.
items.e: Dipole moment and geometry.
items.h: 4(c). Explain, with the help of molecular-orbital theory, the paramagnetic character of oxygen.

items.q: 5(b). How could you measure the dipole moment of a molecule?
items.q2: 5(ب) آپ کسی سالمے کا ڈائی پول مومنٹ کیسے ناپیں گے؟
items.q3: 5(ب) د مالیکول ډایپول مومنټ څنګه اندازه کولای شئ؟
items.a: The dipole moment is measured from the effect of an electric field on the substance: the dielectric constant (capacitance) of the sample in a condenser is measured at different temperatures, and the dipole moment is calculated using the Debye equation; it is expressed in debye (D).
items.e: Experimental determination.

items.q: 5(c). Write down the difference among molecular, network and metallic solids.
items.q2: 5(ج) سالماتی، نیٹ ورک اور دھاتی ٹھوسوں کے درمیان فرق لکھیں۔
items.q3: 5(ج) د مالیکولي، شبکوي او فلزي جامدونو ترمنځ توپیر ولیکئ.
items.a: Molecular solids (ice, iodine, sugar) consist of molecules held by weak van der Waals forces or hydrogen bonds, have low melting points, are soft and non-conductors. Network (covalent) solids (diamond, SiO₂) are held by a continuous network of covalent bonds, very hard with very high melting points, non-conductors (graphite conducts). Metallic solids (Na, Cu) consist of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, are malleable, ductile, shiny and conduct electricity.
items.e: Types of solids.

items.q: Justify that 1cm³ of hydrogen (H₂) and 1cm³ of methane (CH₄) at STP will [scan obscured] same number of molecules although one molecules of methane (CH₄) is 8 [scan obscured] heavier than that of hydrogen (H₂).
items.q2: جواز دیں کہ STP پر ہائیڈروجن (H₂) کے 1cm³ اور میتھین (CH₄) کے 1cm³ میں سالموں کی تعداد برابر [اسکین میں متن چھپا ہوا ہے]، اگرچہ میتھین (CH₄) کا ایک سالمہ ہائیڈروجن (H₂) کے سالمے سے 8 [اسکین میں متن چھپا ہوا ہے] بھاری ہے۔
items.q3: دلیل وړاندې کړئ چې په STP کې د هایدروجن (H₂) په 1cm³ او د میتان (CH₄) په 1cm³ کې د مالیکولونو شمېر یو شان [په سکین کې متن پټ دی]، که څه هم د میتان (CH₄) یو مالیکول د هایدروجن (H₂) تر مالیکول 8 [په سکین کې متن پټ دی] دروند دی.
items.a: By Avogadro's law equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain the same number of molecules, whatever their mass. In a gas the molecules are very far apart, so the volume depends on the number of molecules and not on their size; hence 1 cm³ each of H₂ and CH₄ at STP have the same number of molecules, although a CH₄ molecule (16) is eight times as heavy as an H₂ molecule (2).
items.e: Avogadro's law.

items.q: Do you think that some of the postulates of kinetic molecular theory of ga[scan obscured] are faulty? Write down these postulates.
items.q2: کیا آپ کے خیال میں گیس[اسکین میں متن چھپا ہوا ہے] کے حرکی سالماتی نظریے کے بعض مفروضے ناقص ہیں؟ یہ مفروضے لکھیں۔
items.q3: ایا ستاسو په اند د ګاز[په سکین کې متن پټ دی] د کینټیک مالیکولي تیورۍ ځینې فرضونه ناسم دي؟ دغه فرضونه ولیکئ.
items.a: Yes, some postulates are only approximately true for real gases. Postulates: (1) gases consist of very small particles, widely separated; (2) the particles move randomly in straight lines; (3) collisions are perfectly elastic; (4) there are no attractive or repulsive forces between particles; (5) the actual volume of the molecules is negligible compared to the volume of the gas; (6) the average kinetic energy is proportional to the absolute temperature. Postulates (4) and (5) are faulty: real gases have attraction and finite volume, especially at high pressure and low temperature.
items.e: KMT.

items.q: Why high pressure and low temperature make the gases non-ideal?
items.q2: زیادہ دباؤ اور کم درجہ حرارت گیسوں کو غیر مثالی کیوں بناتے ہیں؟
items.q3: لوړ فشار او ټیټه تودوخه ولې ګازونه غیرمثالي کوي؟
items.a: At high pressure the molecules are forced close together, so their own volume is no longer negligible; at low temperature the molecules move slowly, so the attractive forces become significant. Both factors violate the assumptions of the ideal gas, making the gases non-ideal.
items.e: Real gases.

items.q: What is your opinion about rapid expansion of gases causes cooling?
items.q2: گیسوں کے تیز پھیلاؤ سے ٹھنڈک پیدا ہونے کے بارے میں آپ کی کیا رائے ہے؟
items.q3: د ګازونو د چټکې پراختیا له امله د یخېدو په اړه ستاسو نظر څه دی؟
items.a: When a compressed gas expands rapidly, its molecules do work against the attraction between them; the energy for this comes from their own kinetic energy, so the temperature falls (Joule-Thomson effect). This is why a gas leaving a cylinder becomes cold.
items.e: Cooling by expansion.

items.q: Why do you think that lighter gases can diffuse more rapidly than heavier on[scan obscured]

items.q3: ستاسو په اند سپک ګازونه ولې د درنو [په سکین کې متن پټ دی] په پرتله چټک خپرېدای شي؟
items.a: Lighter gases diffuse faster because at the same temperature all gases have the same average kinetic energy, so lighter molecules have higher speeds; the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass (Graham's law).
items.e: Graham's law.
